Genetic parameters for each group

Source: vignettes/articles/parameters-by-group.Rmd
parameters-by-group.Rmd

中文版

When the data hold several populations, the genetic parameters often differ between them. The usual table is “h2 (SE) of every trait in every group”. With mintyrasr this is one nested table and one call; no cross-validation is needed (cv = NULL, the default).

Data

One row per individual, with the group column (here test_herd), the fixed effects and the traits:

library(asreml)
library(mintyr)
library(mintyrasr)

pheno <- import_xlsx("pheno.xlsx")      # id, test_herd, hhys, sex, adg, bf, fcr

Single-trait parameters per group

w2l_nest(by = "test_herd") makes one data set per trait and group:

nest <- w2l_nest(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), by = "test_herd", out_type = "df")
nest                                     # name | test_herd | data

res <- asr_gblup(nest, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys + sex, inbreeding = inbreeding,
                 path = "h2_by_herd.xlsx")
res$param[, .(name, test_herd, h2, h2_se, status, boundary)]

A report table, traits in rows and groups in columns:

library(data.table)
p <- res$param[, .(name, test_herd, txt = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", h2, h2_se))]
dcast(p, name ~ test_herd, value.var = "txt")

Any model of Beyond the animal model works the same way, e.g. random = ~ litter adds prop_litter per group. Pedigree or single-step analyses only need another matrix (see A, G and H).

All groups together

For comparison, the same traits with all groups in one model; the group effect is in the fixed effects (here through hhys, which is nested in herd):

all <- w2l_nest(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), out_type = "df")
res_all <- asr_gblup(all, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys + sex, inbreeding = inbreeding)
res_all$param[, .(name, h2, h2_se)]

To test whether the genetic variance differs between groups, or how well the groups are genetically connected, see the G x E part of Beyond the animal model and The same trait in different populations.

Two-trait parameters per group

c2p_nest(by = "test_herd") gives every trait pair in every group; see Correlations between traits in each population.

Points to watch

  • Group size. Small groups give large SEs and estimates at the boundary (h2 = 0). Check status, boundary and res$log; a component fixed at the boundary is listed there.
  • Fixed effects per group. Contemporary groups usually differ between groups; with one model per group each group gets its own levels anyway.
  • Same model in all groups, so that the estimates are comparable; if one group needs a different model, run it separately.
  • GEBVs per group are in res$gebv (with reliable = rel >= min_rel).
